item.research_question: How does entropy stabilization in transition-metal-based high entropy oxides (TM-HEO) influence reversible lithium storage capacity, cycling stability, and the underlying reaction mechanism compared to medium entropy oxides?
item.material_system: Transition-metal-based high entropy oxides (TM-HEO) with composition (Co0.2Cu0.2Mg0.2Ni0.2Zn0.2)O; compared to 4-cation medium entropy oxides (MEO) such as (Co0.25Cu0.25Zn0.25Ni0.25)O and (Co0.25Cu0.25Mg0.25Zn0.25)O
item.processing_route: Nebulized Spray Pyrolysis (NSP) at 1150 °C; 4-cation systems required post-annealing at 1000 °C for 1 h under ambient atmosphere; electrodes cast with 63 wt% active material, 22 wt% Super C65, 15 wt% PVA binder
item.test_conditions: Galvanostatic cycling in Li-metal coin cells, voltage range 0.01–3 V vs. Li+/Li, specific currents from 50 to 3000 mA g−1, room temperature, 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC or EC/EMC electrolyte
key_findings: The 5-cation TM-HEO cycled over 300 cycles at 200 mA g−1 with specific capacities stabilizing around 650 mAh g−1 after initial activation.
The 5-cation system achieved a specific capacity of 770 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles following a rate increase to 3 A g−1 for 5 cycles.
Medium entropy oxides (4-cation systems) showed rapid capacity degradation, with the Co-removed variant failing completely after ~10 cycles.
The Coulombic efficiency of the 5-cation TM-HEO stabilized between 99.4% and 99.95% in the range of cycles 60–400.
The 4-cation system without Zn (TM-MEO(-Zn)) exhibited a two-step oxidation process at 1.7 V and 2.2 V, unlike the single-step oxidation of the 5-cation system.
High-loading electrodes (2.3 mg cm−2) maintained Coulombic efficiencies >98.5% and an areal capacity of 1.3 mAh cm−2 after 30 cycles.
No metallic phases or Cu dendrites were detected via TEM/EDX after 100 cycles, despite the conversion reaction mechanism.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the rock-salt structure is preserved as a permanent host matrix during the entire conversion process. While some cations (e.g., Co, Cu) are reduced to metallic states during lithiation, they remain 'trapped' within the defect-rich rock-salt lattice stabilized by unreduced cations (e.g., Mg, Ni). This entropy stabilization lowers the Gibbs free energy, favoring the re-incorporation of reduced cations into the original lattice sites upon delithiation, preventing phase separation and structural collapse.
item.limitations: The theoretical capacity cannot be predicted with high accuracy due to unknown additional processes like Zn-Li alloying or intermetallic formation; some 4-cation systems (TM-MEO(-Mg) and TM-MEO(-Ni)) could not be synthesized as single-phase compounds even at high temperatures.
item.future_work: Further investigations should be pursued to explore the full potential of high entropy oxide electrode materials, including the addition of other cations (Fe, Mn, Cr, V) to develop a modular method for tailoring electrodes to specific needs.
quotes: The stabilization effect of entropy brings significant benefits for the storage capacity retention of high entropy oxides and greatly improves the cycling stability.
The preservation of the rock-salt structure (if only partially) over the entire redox process, is identified as a likely reason for the observed stable cycling behavior.

The re-incorporation of the metal ions into the TM-HEO rock-salt structure at room temperature upon electrochemical cycling, facilitated by high entropy stabilization, is expected to add a new dimension to the traditional conversion based lithiation mechanism.
